message.content:
Below is a concise, practical overview of the key rights you have as a residential tenant in Texas. (This is not legal advice; if you have a specific dispute, consult an attorney or your local tenant‑rights organization.) | Category | What You’re Generally Entitled To | How It’s Enforced | |----------|-----------------------------------|-------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | Texas Property Code §92.001–92.006. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For **month‑to‑month** leases: 30‑day written notice to terminate.
• For **fixed‑term** leases: landlord must give notice before the lease expires if they intend to change terms or not renew. | Texas Property Code §92.001. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity).
• You can withhold rent or repair‑and‑deduct if the landlord fails to maintain habitability. | Texas Property Code §92.011–92.013. | | **Right to Privacy** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hrs) before entering, except in emergencies. | Texas Property Code §92.001. | | **Fair Housing** | • Discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income is prohibited. | Texas Fair Housing Act (Texas Property Code §92.001). | | **Repair‑and‑Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to fix a major problem, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from your rent (up to the amount of the rent). | Texas Property Code §92.013. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but they must give proper notice (usually 30 days for month‑to‑month). | Texas Property Code §92.001. | | **Lease Terms** | • Any lease clause that is **unreasonable, illegal, or contrary to public policy** can be challenged. | Texas Property Code §92.001. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the formal eviction procedure (notice, court filing, judgment). Unlawful “self‑eviction” tactics (e.g., changing locks without a court order) are prohibited. | Texas Property Code §§92.001–92.006. | | **Security Deposit Deductions** | • Landlord may only deduct for: unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear, cleaning beyond normal, and other costs specified in the lease. | Texas Property Code §92.006. | | **Tenant’s Right to Repair** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may:
 1. **Notify** the landlord in writing.
 2. **Give** them a reasonable time to fix.
 3. If they still don’t fix, you may repair and deduct or pursue a claim. | Texas Property Code §92.013. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • You may sublet or assign the lease only if the lease allows it or the landlord consents (which can’t be unreasonably withheld). | Texas Property Code §92.001. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide essential utilities (water, heat, electricity) unless otherwise agreed. | Texas Property Code §92.011. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlord must keep common areas (hallways, elevators, parking lots) safe and clean. | Texas Property Code §92.011. | | **Dispute Resolution** | • You can file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office, the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs, or seek small‑claims court. | Texas Property Code §92.001. | ### Quick Checklist for Your Tenancy 1. **Read the Lease Carefully** – Look for clauses on rent, deposits, maintenance, entry, and termination. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, photos of damages, and maintenance requests. 3. **Know the Notice Periods** – 30 days for month‑to‑month, 60 days for fixed‑term if you’re giving notice. 4. **Report Problems Promptly** – Send a written notice to the landlord and keep a copy. 5. **Keep Records of Repairs** – If you repair something yourself, keep receipts and a written statement of the issue. 6. **Know When to Seek Legal Help** – If the landlord refuses to comply with habitability standards or tries to evict you unlawfully. ### Resources | Resource | What It Offers | Link | |----------|----------------|------| | **Texas Attorney General – Tenant Rights** | Guides, FAQs, and complaint forms. | https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/ | | **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs** | Fair housing enforcement, landlord‑tenant resources. | https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us/ | | **Local Tenant‑Rights Organizations** | Free or low‑cost legal assistance, mediation. | Search “tenant rights Texas” + your city. | | **Texas Property Code** | Full statutory text. | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/ | | **Legal Aid of North Texas** | Free legal help for qualifying tenants. | https://www.lanxt.org/ | --- #### Bottom Line As a Texas tenant, you have the right to a safe, habitable home, a fair security‑deposit process, reasonable notice before entry, and protection against unlawful eviction or discrimination. If a landlord violates these rights, you can take action through written notices, repair‑and‑deduct, or legal remedies such as filing a complaint or suing in small‑claims court. Always keep written records and seek professional help if the situation escalates.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are my rights as a tenant in the state of Texas?" They want information about tenant rights. We can provide a summary. There's no request for a contract generation. So we don't need to call the function. Just answer. Provide general rights: security deposit limits, notice requirements, habitability, right to privacy, right to repair, right to fair housing, etc. Also mention relevant statutes: Texas Property Code, local ordinances. Provide resources. Should be thorough but not too long.
